comment: Mac mini iOS HITL bench catalog — read by hitl-reserved --runner darwin on the Mac (nix/hitl-darwin.nix). Unlike the Linux benches there is NO container: the darwin runner grants each reservation a scoped SSH login into the shared daemon user, and the iPhone (devicectl/usbmux), the Simulator (simctl), and each C6 (esptool over /dev/cu.usbmodem*) are reached host-native from that session. So components carry NO 'devices' mounts (nothing to bind into a container); hardware is selected by env markers (a serial port, a UDID) instead. Two independent units, each with its OWN C6 (user decision: two C6s/location). host/workspace + the unit sshd-port range are passed as flags by hitl-darwin.nix, not baked here. NOTE: the iPhone UDID and the two C6 serial ports below are PLACEHOLDERS — fill them from the live Mac (`xcrun xctrace list devices` for the UDID; `ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*` / esptool for the C6 ports) before the first deploy, same as the amd-rig catalogs were filled against the live rig.

components.comment: The real-iPhone unit's C6 DUT, reached host-native by esptool over its USB-serial port (macOS names it /dev/cu.usbmodem<N>). No 'devices' mount — the darwin runner has no container. HITL_ESP_PORT pins the port the toolbox targets; HITL_ADAPTER_SERIAL selects the board's USB-JTAG for any openocd/gdb use. PLACEHOLDER port + serial — fill from the live Mac.
components.name: c6-c

components.comment: The Simulator unit's C6 DUT (second board). Same host-native esptool path. PLACEHOLDER port + serial — fill from the live Mac.
components.name: c6-d

components.comment: The iOS dev device: a real iPhone reached host-native via CoreDevice (devicectl) + usbmux — NOT a USB passthrough (the darwin runner has no container). Carries no device node, just the env markers: HITL_IOS_UDID selects this exact iPhone for devicectl build/install/launch (tools/ios_build_server.py); HITL_PHONE_TARGET routes phone_e2e to the iOS-device lane. PLACEHOLDER UDID — fill from `xcrun xctrace list devices` on the Mac.
components.name: ios-dev

units.comment: REAL-iPHONE unit: the iPhone + its C6. The client reserves it (scoped SSH into the Mac daemon user), ships the phone-HITL harness + web bundle, and runs phone_e2e --phone-target ios-phone: builds/installs the Capacitor app on the real iPhone via devicectl (ios_build_server), opens it at ?driver=…&ble=real, and the PHONE provisions the real C6 over CoreBluetooth (Capacitor Improv plugin) → maps/solves end to end. Not pin_only: a bare `--require-caps ios-device,real-ble` request should match it.
units.name: ios-phone

units.comment: SIMULATOR unit: a C6 + the iOS Simulator (no dedicated hardware — simctl boots a simulated iPhone on the shared Mac). The env builds/installs the app on the Simulator via simctl (ios_build_server), drives it at the Mac-host alias, and connects the forwarded real-C6 wss for the map/solve. BLE has no Simulator backend, so onboarding uses the app-seam virtual mock or the Bumble peripheral (ble_peripheral.py), not real CoreBluetooth. pin_only so a caps-only request never lands the Simulator slot.
units.name: ios-sim
